---
title: "plot2 for ggplot2 users"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.2,
  dpi = 72,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(plot2)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

This article is for users who know `ggplot2`. It describes how the concepts of `plot2()` relate to those of `ggplot2`, and what `plot2()` does by default.

## Concepts

`ggplot2` builds a plot from components: data, aesthetic mappings, geoms, statistics, scales, coordinates, facets and a theme. `plot2()` builds the same components, but its arguments describe the plot instead of the components:

| `plot2()` | `ggplot2` |
|:----------|:----------|
| `x`, `y` | `aes(x = , y = )` |
| `category` | `aes(colour = )` or `aes(fill = )`, depending on the geom; or another aesthetic set with `category.type` |
| `facet` | `facet_wrap()` |
| `type` | `geom_*()`, together with the position, such as `position_dodge()` |
| calculations in `x`, `y`, `category` and `facet` | `group_by()` and `summarise()` or `mutate()` before the plot |
| `x.sort`, `category.sort`, `facet.sort` | `forcats::fct_reorder()`, `fct_infreq()` or `fct_relevel()` before the plot |
| `x.max_items`, `category.max_items` | `forcats::fct_lump_n()` before the plot |
| `colour`, `colour_fill` | `scale_colour_*()` and `scale_fill_*()` |
| `x.*` and `y.*` settings | `scale_x_*()` and `scale_y_*()` |
| `datalabels` | `geom_text()` or `geom_label()` with the summarised values |
| `title`, `x.title`, `category.title`, ... | `labs()` |
| `theme` | `theme_*()` and `theme()` |

## An example

This plot shows the number of admissions per hospital and gender, sorted by the total number of admissions, with data labels. In `ggplot2`, the data are summarised and sorted first:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  count(hospital, gender) |>
  mutate(hospital = reorder(hospital, -n, FUN = sum)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hospital, y = n, fill = gender)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), vjust = -0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Hospital", y = "Admissions", fill = "Gender") +
  theme_minimal()
```

In `plot2()`, the same steps are arguments:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital,
        y = n(),
        category = gender,
        x.sort = "freq-desc",
        x.title = "Hospital",
        y.title = "Admissions",
        category.title = "Gender")
```

The results differ in style, because each package has its own defaults; the next section lists those of `plot2()`.

## Defaults of plot2()

`plot2()` sets these defaults, each of which can be changed with the argument concerned:

- The theme is `theme_minimal2()` (argument `theme`; `theme = NULL` uses the default theme of `ggplot2`).
- The y axis starts at zero where possible and has extra room at the top (`y.zoom`, `y.limits` and `y.expand`).
- Column plots have data labels when there are at most 25 columns (`datalabels`).
- The legend is at the top, or at the right for a numeric `category` (`legend.position`).
- Text and factor values of `x` are sorted alphabetically, with numbers in their numeric order (`x.sort`).
- Whole numbers that look like years or months become text in discrete plot types (`x.character` and `category.character`).
- Large and small numbers on the y axis are formatted with a thousands separator or in scientific notation (`y.scientific`, `big.mark` and `decimal.mark`).
- Axis titles are taken from the given columns or calculations (`x.title`, `y.title`, `category.title`).

The section *Automatic choices* in `?plot2` lists all rules, and in an interactive session `plot2()` reports each decision in a message.

## Continuing with ggplot2

`plot2()` returns a `ggplot` object, so every `ggplot2` function can be added to it:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = age, type = "histogram", binwidth = 5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 65, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 64, y = 40, label = "Aged 65 and over", hjust = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 10))
```

A scale that `plot2()` already set is replaced, with a message from `ggplot2`. Use the `x.*` and `y.*` arguments of `plot2()` to avoid this.

The package also has functions to change a plot afterwards:

- `add_type()` adds any geom with the data of the plot, and `add_line()`, `add_point()`, `add_col()`, `add_errorbar()`, `add_smooth()` and `add_sf()` add the most common ones;
- `add_mapping()` adds or changes an aesthetic mapping;
- `move_layer()` changes the order of the layers;
- `get_plot_title()` returns the title of a plot, for example to use it as a file name.

## Using parts of plot2 with ggplot2

Several functions of `plot2` also work in plots made with `ggplot2` alone:

- `theme_minimal2()`, the theme;
- `coord_spider()`, the coordinate system of spider plots;
- `get_colour()`, which returns colours from palettes and registered colours, for example for `scale_fill_manual(values = get_colour("viridis", 4))`;
- `md_to_expression()`, which converts markdown to a `plotmath` expression for titles and labels;
- the labelling functions `euros()`, `dollars()` and `label_taxonomy()`, for scales and data labels.

```{r}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = get_colour("Tableau 10", 3)) +
  labs(colour = "Cylinders") +
  theme_minimal2()
```
